newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour government names more ministers.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour government names more ministers.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government named a whole host of second-tier ministerial appointments on Monday, Downing Street officials said.

Stephen Byers, formerly Labour's employment spokesman, was named minister of state for Education in charge of school standards while Baroness Blackstone is Education minister in charge of further and higher education.
Tessa Jowell and Alan Milburn are named as Health ministers of state. In opposition, Jowell had been deputy health spokeswoman while Milburn was a Treasury spokesman.
John Reid has been appointed defence minister of state while Derek Fatchett and Tony Lloyd become Foreign Office ministers of state.
Henry McLeish becomes a Scottish Office minister of state and Alun Michael and Joyce Quin are appointed Home Office ministers of state.
At the Department of Trade and Industry, John Battle and Ian McCartney are named as ministers of state. Environment and Transport ministers of state are Dick Caborn and Hilary Armstrong.
Junior Minister at the Lord Chancellor's Department is Geoff Hoon. He had been in charge of Labour's Business Relations Unit, charged with wooing business and City leaders.
Peter Hain, veteran anti-apartheid campaigner and MP for the Welsh constituency of Neath, is named junior minister for Wales.
A Downing Street official said there would be more appointments to come but the next official news release would be a list of the complete government line-up.
